summary: Medici is a fast, tense once-around auction game where players bid points (not money) on lots of 1-3 goods cards to fill their ships; over three rounds you're weighing how much a lot is worth against how many bidding turns you have left. It's lighter and quicker than most Knizia auction games, with a satisfying push-your-luck feel to timing your bids and gauging when to let a lot pass to the next player.
praised: Quick, tight auction mechanism that's easy to teach
Interesting tension since points are the bidding currency, not separate money
Short playtime with real decisions each turn
Classic Knizia elegance and depth from simple rules
criticised: Can feel a bit dry or abstract thematically (cards are just commodities)
Luck of the card reveals can swing outcomes
Some find the scoring math (majorities plus cargo value) fiddly to track
Less depth than some other Knizia auction titles like Ra or Modern Art

interaction.kind: competitive bidding where every point spent denies future bids

scoring.why: Winner is decided by round-end majority bonuses in specific commodities plus total cargo value, so a couple of commodity types you focus on drive most of your score

similar: Fits (or Medici vs. Strozzi for the 2-player version)
